title: Orchestrated rollout policy engine & traffic guardrails
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a policy-driven rollout engine that expresses multi-step traffic splits, conditional progression rules, automated rollback triggers, and shadow traffic modes. This ticket covers the control-plane config model, core evaluation logic, integration points with router/runtime, console UI hooks for step previews, and telemetry/alerting guardrails. Goal: let product/engineering teams declare canaries with safety checks (latency/error/regression thresholds), step schedules (time-based and metric-based), and automatic rollback if hurtful regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: A declarative rollout spec format exists and is validated in the control plane (YAML/JSON) and exposed via API
Traffic split engine can apply multi-step percentages and switch snapshots atomically across model variants
Progression rules support both time-based and metric-based transitions (e.g., 15m OR <0.5% error increase)
Rollback policy triggers on configurable signals (p50/p95 latency regressions, error rate increase, custom signals) and performs automatic failover to previous stable model
Console shows step timeline, live traffic splits, and 'what-if' preview before applying a rollout
Integrations with tracing/metrics (Datadog/Grafana) emit verifiable rollout events and guardrail alerts
E2E test harness simulates noisy traffic and verifies automatic rollback works reliably in CI
updates: 2025-01-15: RFC drafted and shared in #model-lifecycle. High-level schema includes steps, predicates, rollbackActions, and shadowMode. Link to RFC: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/rlf-canary-policy

2025-01-22: Design review with runtime and console teams — decided to keep control-plane evaluation deterministic and push metric evaluation to a separate policy worker to avoid adding latency in data path

2025-01-30: Prototype of rollout spec validator completed. Initial spec: name, baseline_model, candidate_model, steps [{percent, min_duration, predicates}], rollback {triggers, backoff}, metadata. Validator PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/411

2025-02-04: Implementation spike shows kernel scheduling and routing sidecar can accept atomic split updates via the existing route-api with minor extension (route-version header). Created PR in runtime: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1234

2025-02-10: Telemetry schema for rollout metrics agreed (rollout_id, step_index, applied_percent, guardrail_signals). Drafted dashboard template: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rollouts/rollout-overview

2025-02-12: Began integration tests for metric-based progression using synthetic traffic generator. Found a corner case where transient spikes cause oscillation — added hysteresis and min_stable_window to progression rules
review_feedback: PM (Rafael Ortiz): prefer conservative defaults for progression (longer min_duration) and explicit opt-in to automatic rollback for enterprise customers
Design (Priya Singh): console needs a compact timeline visualization and pre-apply diff to show how traffic will change across routes
Security (Anita Rao): require audit events for all rollout state transitions and restrict who can execute automatic rollback via RBAC
Runtime (Jared Kim): avoid synchronous metric lookups during request routing; metrics evaluation must be eventually consistent and idempotent
next_steps: Complete policy worker that ingests metric streams and evaluates predicates
Wire validator into control plane API and add RBAC checks for rollout execution
Implement atomic split update path in runtime route-api and validate with integration tests
Add audit events and retention policy for rollout lifecycle events
Ship basic console UX for creating managed canaries with sensible defaults and enterprise toggles
